alignments.note: `אִם לֹא` rendered by the single *Surely*, which carries both morphemes' sense, so they share one unit under rule 30. Neither particle carries content the other lacks, so rule 23's syntactic-head direction puts the source head on the first morpheme; the competing reading heads on the negative.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun and auxiliary under rule 17, headed on the lexical verb.
Second finite verb; the subject and auxiliary are written once for the coordination and stand with the first verb.

Anarthrous passive participle used substantivally, with the supplied generic *child* and the indefinite article the nominal expression licenses (rules 46 and 15); headed on *weaned*, the word carrying the lexeme, since *child* alone is any child.

The comparative phrase is the predicate of this verbless clause and `נַפְשִׁי` its subject, so the construction-supplied copula joins the preposition heading the predicate under rule 49; the unit is discontinuous around the substantive under rule 25. The competing reading puts *is* on the subject noun, but rule 20 sends the copula to the predicate wherever a predicate morpheme stands.

Article assimilated into the pointed preposition and supplied by MACULA as a token; the ASV writes *a weaned child* with no *the*, so it is unrepresented under rules 12 and 29. The indefinite *a* is the nominal expression's own under rule 15.
Substantival passive participle with its supplied generic noun and indefinite article, read exactly as the first occurrence and headed on *weaned*.
Suffix realized by the object pronoun *me* (rule 18).
Construct noun rendered *soul*, the clause's subject.

review_notes: The two `גָמֻל` phrases are aligned independently and identically; the article morpheme stands only in the second and is unrepresented there.
The copula of the final colon is placed on the comparative preposition under rule 49, the Hebrew clause making `נַפְשִׁי` the subject despite the ASV's English order.
